response.rationale: C1 is the most complete diagnosis: the MRI directly demonstrates bilateral facial nerve enhancement compatible with bilateral facial neuritis, matching the bilateral lower motor neuron facial weakness. R2 has the same core diagnosis but omits the bilateral distribution in its label. R3 is only a descriptive exam finding, while R1 and R4 are unrelated prior chemotherapy side effects.

rejected.why: Lower motor neuron disease is a syndromic description of the exam finding, not the imaging-confirmed diagnosis, and lacks facial nerve specificity.
Capillary leak syndrome explains prior edema and gemcitabine discontinuation but not the current bilateral facial weakness or facial nerve enhancement.
Grade 1 peripheral neuropathy was stable and does not explain bilateral facial nerve enhancement or facial neuritis.
